title: New Delhi’s Jantar Mantar Is Not Tahrir Square, But It Can Become One
gist: A student protest movement called the Cockroach Janta Party, which originated on Instagram, has mobilized thousands at New Delhi's Jantar Mantar over a leaked National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) exam paper and an associated wave of student suicides. The author judges comparisons to Cairo's Tahrir Square only partly valid, while noting the shared mechanism of social-media-driven mass assembly.

insights.claim: The Cockroach Janta Party, a movement that emerged on Instagram, has used social media to mobilize thousands of protesters to assemble at New Delhi's Jantar Mantar.
insights.speaker: Asif Ullah Khan
insights.so_what: Platform-native political movements can reach street-scale mobilization in India without party infrastructure, raising regulatory and platform-liability risk for social networks operating there.
insights.locator: Likewise, the Cockroach Janta Party, which emerged on Instagram

insights.claim: Egypt's Tahrir Square uprising and the current New Delhi student protests share the same structural mechanism: calls to gather spread rapidly through social platforms — YouTube and Facebook in Egypt's case, Instagram in India's.
insights.speaker: Asif Ullah Khan
insights.so_what: A repeatable template for reading protest escalation risk: watch platform-level virality of assembly calls as the leading indicator rather than formal opposition activity.
insights.quote: In Egypt, calls to gather at Tahrir Square spread rapidly through social media, including YouTube and Facebook.
insights.locator: In Egypt, calls to gather at Tahrir Square

insights.claim: The proximate grievance driving the New Delhi student protests is the leak of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) examination paper, which has fueled widespread anger among students.
insights.speaker: Asif Ullah Khan
insights.so_what: Examination-integrity failures are becoming a politically combustible fault line in India, with implications for education-sector policy and testing administration.
insights.locator: protest against the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) examination paper leak

insights.claim: The protest movement attributes a tragic wave of student suicides to the NEET paper leak, which is the emotional core of its mobilization case.
insights.speaker: Asif Ullah Khan
insights.so_what: The suicide framing is what converts an administrative scandal into sustained street mobilization, which is the escalation channel to monitor.
insights.quote: contributed to a tragic wave of student suicides
insights.locator: which has fueled widespread anger among students

insights.claim: Equating the New Delhi Jantar Mantar student protests with Egypt's Tahrir Square uprising is unrealistic, and the comparison is only partly valid even though the two movements share striking similarities.
insights.speaker: Asif Ullah Khan
insights.so_what: Tempers regime-change extrapolation from Indian protest headlines; the base case is a contained single-issue movement, not a systemic political rupture.
insights.quote: The comparison, however, is only partly valid.
insights.locator: The comparison, however, is only partly valid

insights.claim: The Tahrir Square benchmark is defined by an uprising that ended Hosni Mubarak's nearly 30-year rule, setting a very high bar that the Jantar Mantar protests have not met.
insights.speaker: Asif Ullah Khan
insights.so_what: Useful calibration for pricing political risk: the analogy only becomes actionable if the movement broadens beyond a single exam grievance.
insights.locator: the epicenter of the uprising that brought to an end
